name: Rivendell
note: Fan work from Tolkien, whose work belongs to the Tolkien Estate; nothing from any book, film or game is used, and every shape here is this project's own geometry. Made after Tolkien's text and his own drawings of the place (used for proportion and arrangement only). The valley runs east-west, as the books have it: the house is on a shelf on the north side, its windows looking south across the ravine; the head of the valley is east, towards the mountains; the Ford is downstream to the west. The ground, the river line and the plan are generated by tools/make-rivendell.py; the house, the water, the woods and the rest are src/rivendell/. Positions are [lat, lon] against an origin in the valley.
defaultView: Into the valley, from the edge
attribution: Rivendell is fan work: geometry generated by tools/make-rivendell.py and src/rivendell/, after Tolkien's text and drawings. Tolkien's world belongs to the Tolkien Estate. No assets used.

landmarks.name: The Last Homely House
landmarks.info: Not a palace and not a fortress: a house, unfortified in its valley. A long range of two storeys under a steep red roof, a square tower with a hipped roof at its west end, and a loggia of slender columns and gently curved arches along the front, looking south across the ravine to the falls. The porch on the east side opens onto the gardens, where the Council was held.

landmarks.name: The Hall of Fire
landmarks.info: One tall room in the north wing, with a fire in it all the year round and carven pillars on either side of each hearth. On high days there is singing and telling of tales; on other days it stands empty and quiet, and people come there alone to think.

landmarks.name: The tower
landmarks.info: The square tower at the west end of the house, taller than anything else in the valley, with a hipped roof and a balcony over the river. It is in all of Tolkien's drawings of the place.

landmarks.name: The bridge
landmarks.info: 'A narrow bridge of stone without a parapet, as narrow as a pony could well walk on': one arch over the Bruinen, below the house. Everyone who comes in from the Ford crosses here.

landmarks.name: The stair in the rock
landmarks.info: The way in from the Ford goes along the south side of the valley floor and over a rock, by a stair cut into the stone, and down to the bridge.

landmarks.name: The terrace pavilion
landmarks.info: Eight slender columns, a dome gone green and a seat round the inside, at the edge of the shelf where it drops to the water: a place to sit with the noise of the river under you.

landmarks.name: The east pavilion
landmarks.info: Another of the pavilions on the edge of the shelf, looking across to the falls on the south wall.

landmarks.name: The garden seat
landmarks.info: At the far end of the east garden, where the path along the river gives out.

landmarks.name: The stables and the forge
landmarks.info: Behind the house to the north-east: long low stables under a red roof, and the forge where Narsil was made again.

landmarks.name: The falls
landmarks.info: Every stream on the moor comes over the rim: it runs across the heather, cascades down through the firs under the edge, and slides down the rock to the floor of the valley. This one is across the river from the house, and it is what the terrace looks at.

landmarks.name: The Bruinen
landmarks.info: The Loudwater: 'flowing fast and noisily, as mountain-streams do'. It comes down out of the mountains at the head of the valley in rapids, runs past the house, goes over a fall below the bridge and away west to the Ford.

landmarks.name: The zig-zag path
landmarks.info: The way Bilbo came in: over the moor, to 'the edge of a steep fall in the ground', and 'down the steep zig-zag path into the secret valley', through a break in the south wall.

landmarks.name: The Ford of Bruinen
landmarks.info: Where the East Road crosses the river, downstream to the west. The valley's defence is not a wall: it is that anything coming down the road has to stand in the river to get in.

life._: lanterns along the paths and the terrace, smoke from the hearths, leaves on the river in autumn, birds over the valley
